newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to meet Maastricht criteria - wise men.
newsitem.headline: Spain to meet Maastricht criteria - wise men.

text.p: Spain's wise men, a group of independent economists advising the Economy Ministry, said on Wednesday Spain would meet European convergence criteria in 1997 and enter the first wave of the single currency in 1999.
"European economic and monetary union will start as forecast and Spain will meet the criteria required to be part of it," the experts said in a report published today.
It added Spain was one of the best-performing countries in the run-up to the single currency.
"Spain is now one of the countries with the best results in terms of convergence among candidates for the euro," they added.
Spain already meets two criteria regarding forex exchange stability and long term interest rate spreads.
Before the end of the year, they added, it would also "easily meet inflation and public budget criteria".
The fifth criterion, which requires public debt being lower than 60 percent of gross domestic product, would not be respected but the percentage would show a fall.
"(This ratio) will show a decline versus the 1996 value, allowing Spain to enter (EMU)" they added.
